description.narrative:
Uganda has continued to benefit from the various development assistance from developed countries. Key sectors such as health are sufficiently funded by the external support to about 41% of the total expenditures. In additional to this support, more external support in terms of debts have been acquired by the government from both multinational and bilateral lenders. The provisional total public debt stock (in nominal terms) at the end of February 2022 for instance stood at Shs.74,434.3 billion, a 6.8 percent increase from June 2021 compared to an increase of 16.3 percent the same period last year. This however doesn’t negate several debt reliefs the Uganda received in early 1990s and in 2006 through the the Highly Indebted Poor Countries (HIPCs) initiative, and the Multilateral Debt Relief Initiative (MDRI) respectively . Increased public debt and its related obligations in terms of interest payments has thus deprived the available government budget to finance its sectors. For instance over the last 5 financial years, interest payments on the public debt has been the first funding priority for government compared to other sectors such as education, health ,agriculture among others. This has a large implication on service delivery to citizens as financial resources that would be invested in critical public service deliverables are eroded by the debt obligations. According to Oxfam’s CRI index report 2021, EastAfrican countries were spending five times as much on domestic and external debt servicing as on health. This clearly imply that increase public debt negatively affect the poor who mostly rely on public amenities.
Against this background, OXFAM in Uganda ,plan to implement two media engagement activities in which insights from the CRI report will be shared with stakeholders for policy actions. These insights are planned to speak to the current realities including the inflationary pressure, raising cost of living, unpaid workforce, increasing public debt, government expenditure on poverty reducing sectors among others.
Specifically, themedia engagement activities are aimed at: 1. Influencing public narrative on the commitments of government to address inequality in Uganda 2. Increasing citizens demand for downward accountability.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project’s implementation.
